title: Queen Srimala
hookLine: a queen teaches before the Buddha, and he approves (Srimaladevi Sutra)

cards: A letter arrives at a palace in Ayodhya. It's from the queen's parents, King Prasenajit and Queen Mallika. They have met the Buddha, they write, and they want their daughter to know about him too.

Queen Srimala reads it, and something in her opens. She answers not with a letter but with verses of praise, spoken aloud, and in the sutra the Buddha appears in the sky over the palace to hear her. Then the surprise.
She doesn't just listen. She teaches, and he says, go on.

teach.h: HER VOWS: NO ANGER, NO HOARDING.
teach.b: Before she teaches anything, Srimala makes vows in front of the Buddha, and they are strikingly practical. Not to give way to anger toward any being. Not to envy what others have.
Not to hoard for herself. And when she meets the lonely, the imprisoned, the sick and the poor, not to walk away until she has helped.

Then she asks permission to speak, and he gives it. In the sutra the queen does most of the talking. The Buddha's part is often to listen and approve, saying, in substance, excellent, excellent, just so.
Her subject is large: holding fast to the true teaching, that the many vehicles of the path are finally one, and the Buddha-nature hidden in beings, the same gold from yesterday's rags.
A laywoman, a married queen, sets out weighty Mahayana teaching, and the sutra shows the Buddha confirming it point by point.
Then the title: the Lion's Roar of Queen Srimala. The lion's roar is a phrase Buddhist texts use for the Buddha's own fearless teaching.
Here it is given to her. She closes a week that ran from the storehouse of seeds through the healing Buddha, Ksitigarbha's vow, Jizo by the road, Avalokiteshvara listening and the gold in rags.
Srimala ends it with a voice: she speaks, and the Buddha lets her.

how: The Srimaladevi Sutra is studied in East Asian Buddhism, especially in teaching on Buddha-nature, and Srimala is remembered as a lay teacher who preached in the Buddha's presence.

games.q: you're Srimala. the Buddha has appeared and heard your praise and your vows. what do you do next?
o: send a letter back to your parents
games.why: she asks to speak, he agrees, and much of the sutra is her teaching, approved by the Buddha.

practice: Bring to mind a woman who taught you something that stayed, a grandmother, a teacher, a nurse, a boss, a friend, whether a skill, a way of speaking or a way of carrying trouble. Let her face come clearly, and notice what she gave.
If you pray, hold her in that prayer; if you don't, simply hold her in mind with thanks for a while.

wordCard.voice: Queen Srimala. In the Srimaladevi Sutra, the laywoman and queen who teaches before the Buddha, and whose teaching he approves. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the queen's name, from the sutra's title, the Lion's Roar of Queen Srimala.

carryVoice: Your line: the queen teaches. In this sutra, the lion's roar is hers. That's the week, complete.
